item.title: Impetigo Closures, Police Shooting Award, Tax Reform
item.ns0:title: Impetigo Closures, Police Shooting Award, Tax Reform
item.description:
Tonight on Our News, two local schools are temporarily closed for cleaning following confirmed cases of impetigo, prompting health officials to advise parents on recognizing the contagious skin infection. A man paralyzed by a police bullet a decade ago breaks his silence after being awarded over $800,000 in court damages, while the Court of Appeal upholds the decision to deny bail to a suspect in the murder of former parliamentarian Donald Saunders. Meanwhile, the Chamber of Commerce pushes for fairer taxation and cost-cutting after an international rating agency disputes the government's projected budget surplus. Plus, we bring you details on a major $20 million investment in Commonwealth Brewery, unofficial results in the BPSU leadership election, and highlights from Hands for Hunger’s Paradise Plates fundraiser.
